chunks: So the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If the menstruating woman wants to perform ghusl, then let her insert a piece of cotton. If anything of blood comes out on it, then she should not perform ghusl. But if she does not see anything, then let her perform ghusl. And if after that she sees yellowish discharge, then let her perform wudu and pray.

key_terms.الدَّمِ: blood indicating menstruation is still present
key_terms.صُفْرَةً: yellowish discharge seen after apparent purity
key_terms.قُطْنَةً: a piece of cotton used here to check for remaining blood

ai.seo_question: How does a menstruating woman determine when to perform ghusl and resume prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about determining the end of menstruation before performing ghusl. It explains that the presence or absence of blood is the criterion, and that yellowish discharge seen afterward does not prevent prayer, though wudu is to be performed.
